spots.name: Hagia Sophia
spots.summary: Hagia Sophia, officially the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, is a mosque and a major cultural and historical site in Istanbul, Turkey. It was formerly a church (360–1453) and a museum (1935–2020).

spots.name: Galata Tower
spots.summary: The Galata Tower, officially the Galata Tower Museum, is a medieval Genoese tower in the Galata part of the Beyoğlu district of Istanbul, Turkey. Built as a watchtower at the highest point of the mostly demolished Walls of Galata, the tower is now an exhibition space and museum, and a symbol of Beyoğlu and Istanbul.

spots.name: Blue Mosque, Istanbul
spots.summary: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque, popularly known as the Blue Mosque, is an Ottoman-era historical imperial mosque located in Istanbul, Turkey. It was constructed between 1609 and 1617 during the rule of Ahmed I. It attracts a large number of tourists and is one of the most iconic and popular monuments of Ottoman architecture.

names.ja: スルタンアフメト・モスク

spots.name: Topkapı Palace

hours.note: Closed Tue

spots.summary: The Topkapı Palace or the Seraglio, is a large museum and library in the east of the Fatih district of Istanbul in Turkey. From the 1460s to the completion of Dolmabahçe Palace in 1853, it served as the administrative center of the Ottoman Empire, and was the main residence of its sultans.

spots.name: Constantinople

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Constantinople, the modern Istanbul, was the capital of the Roman Empire and Byzantine Empire from 330 until its takeover by the Ottoman Empire in 1453. After this, it continued to function as the Ottoman capital until the abolition of the Ottoman sultanate in 1922.

names.ja: コンスタンティノープル

spots.name: Dolmabahçe Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Dolmabahçe Palace is a 19th-century imperial palace located in Istanbul, Turkey, along the European shore of the Bosporus, which served as the main administrative center of the Ottoman Empire from 1853 to 1887 and from 1909 to 1922.

spots.name: Süleymaniye Mosque
spots.summary: The Süleymaniye Mosque is an Ottoman imperial mosque located on the Third Hill of Istanbul, Turkey. The mosque was commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent and designed by the imperial architect Mimar Sinan.

names.ja: スレイマニエ・モスク

spots.name: Obelisk of Theodosius
spots.summary: The Obelisk of Theodosius is the Ancient Egyptian obelisk of Pharaoh Thutmose III, first erected around 1450 BC. It was re-erected in the Hippodrome of Constantinople by the Roman emperor Theodosius I in 390.

names.ja: テオドシウスのオベリスク

spots.name: Great Palace of Constantinople

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Great Palace of Constantinople, also known as the Sacred Palace, was the large imperial Byzantine palace complex located in the south-eastern end of the peninsula today making up the Fatih district of Istanbul, in modern Turkey.

names.ja: コンスタンティノープル大宮殿

spots.name: Fatih Mosque, Istanbul

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Fatih Mosque is an Ottoman mosque off Fevzi Paşa Caddesi in the Fatih district of Istanbul, Turkey. The original mosque was constructed between 1463 and 1470 on the site of the Church of the Holy Apostles. Seriously damaged in the 1766 earthquake, it was rebuilt in 1771 to a different design.

names.ja: ファーティフ・モスク

spots.name: Sublime Porte
spots.summary: The Sublime Porte, also known as the Ottoman Porte or High Porte, was a metonymy used to refer collectively to the central government of the Ottoman Empire in Istanbul.

spots.name: Byzantium

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Byzantium or Byzantion was an ancient Greek city in classical antiquity that became known as Constantinople in late antiquity and Istanbul in modern times.

spots.name: Şehzade Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Şehzade Mosque is a 16th-century Ottoman imperial mosque located in the district of Fatih, on the third hill of Istanbul, Turkey. It was commissioned by Suleiman the Magnificent as a memorial to his son Şehzade Mehmed who died in 1543.

names.ja: シェフザード・モスク

spots.name: Basilica Cistern
spots.summary: The Basilica Cistern, or Cisterna Basilica, is the largest of several hundred ancient cisterns that lie beneath the city of Istanbul, Turkey.

names.ja: イスタンブル地下宮殿

spots.name: Grand Bazaar

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Grand Bazaar in Istanbul is one of the largest and oldest covered markets in the world, with 61 covered streets and over 4,000 shops on a total area of 30,700 m2, attracting between 250,000 and 400,000 visitors daily.

spots.name: Bosphorus Bridge
spots.summary: The Bosphorus Bridge, known officially as the 15 July Martyrs Bridge and colloquially as the First Bridge, is the oldest and southernmost of the three suspension bridges spanning the Bosphorus strait in Istanbul, Turkey, thus connecting Europe and Asia. The bridge extends between Ortaköy and Beylerbeyi.

spots.name: Runic inscriptions in Hagia Sophia
spots.summary: There are at least two runic inscriptions in Hagia Sophia's marble parapets. They may have been engraved by members of the Varangian Guard in Constantinople during the Viking Age.

names.ru: Рунические надписи в соборе Святой Софии

spots.name: Eyüp Sultan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Eyüp Sultan Mosque is a mosque in Eyüp district of Istanbul, Turkey. The mosque complex includes a mausoleum marking the spot where Ebu Eyüp el-Ansari, the standard-bearer and companion of the prophet Muhammad, is said to have been buried.

names.ja: エユップスルタンモスク

spots.name: Istanbul Archaeology Museums
spots.summary: The Istanbul Archaeology Museums are a group of three archaeological museums located in the Eminönü quarter of Istanbul, Turkey, near Gülhane Park and Topkapı Palace. These museums house over one million objects from nearly all periods and civilizations in world history.

names.ja: イスタンブル考古学博物館
names.zh: 伊斯坦布尔考古博物馆

spots.name: Serpent Column
spots.summary: The Serpent Column, also known as the Serpentine Column, Plataean Tripod or Delphi Tripod, is an ancient bronze column at the Hippodrome of Constantinople in what is now Istanbul, Turkey.

photo.author: Gryffindor This panoramic image was created with Autostitch (stitched images may

spots.name: Taksim Square
spots.summary: Taksim Square, situated in Beyoğlu in the European part of Istanbul, Turkey, is a major tourist and leisure district famed for its restaurants, shops, and hotels. It is considered the heart of modern Istanbul, with the central station of the Istanbul Metro network.

spots.name: Historic Areas of Istanbul
spots.summary: The Historic Areas of Istanbul are a group of sites in the capital district of Fatih in the city of Istanbul, Turkey. These areas were added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1985.

names.ja: イスタンブール歴史地域

photo.author: please put the following link as a backlink in your article: Istanbul Tipps - Pi

spots.name: Maiden's Tower
spots.summary: The Maiden's Tower, also known as Leander's Tower since the Byzantine period, is a tower on a small islet at the southern entrance of the Bosphorus strait, 200 m (220 yd) from the coast of Üsküdar in Istanbul, Turkey.

spots.name: New Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The New Mosque and later New Valide Sultan Mosque after its partial reconstruction and completion between 1660 and 1665, is an Ottoman imperial mosque located in the Eminönü quarter of Istanbul, Turkey.

spots.name: Hagia Irene

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hagia Irene or Hagia Eirene, sometimes known also as Saint Irene, is a former Eastern Orthodox church located in the outer courtyard of Topkapı Palace in Istanbul.

spots.name: Walls of Constantinople
spots.summary: The walls of Constantinople are a series of defensive stone walls that have surrounded and protected the city of Constantinople since its founding as the new capital of the Roman Empire by Constantine the Great.

names.ja: コンスタンティノープルの城壁

photo.author: The original uploader was -jha- at German Wikipedia.

spots.name: Rüstem Pasha Mosque
spots.summary: The Rüstem Pasha Mosque is an Ottoman mosque located in the Hasırcılar Çarşısı in the Tahtakale neighborhood of the Fatih district of Istanbul, Turkey, near the Spice Bazaar.

names.ja: リュステム・パシャ・モスク

spots.name: Golden Horn
spots.summary: The Golden Horn is a major urban waterway and the primary inlet of the Bosphorus in Istanbul, Turkey. The Golden Horn connects with the Bosphorus Strait at the point where the strait meets the Sea of Marmara.

spots.name: Ortaköy Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ortaköy Mosque, formally the Büyük Mecidiye Camii in Beşiktaş, Istanbul, Turkey, is a mosque situated at the waterside of the Ortaköy pier square, one of the most popular locations on the Bosphorus. It was commissioned by the Ottoman sultan Abdülmecid I, and its construction was completed around 1854 or 1856.

spots.name: Church of the Holy Apostles

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Holy Apostles, also known as the Imperial Polyandrion, was a Byzantine Eastern Orthodox church in Constantinople, capital of the Eastern Roman Empire. The first structure dated to the 4th century, though future emperors would add to and improve upon it.

photo.author: Meister der Predigten des Mönchs Johannes Kokkinobaphos

spots.name: Kafes

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kafes, literally "cage", was the part of the Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Palace where possible successors to the throne were kept under a form of house-arrest and constant surveillance by the palace guards.

photo.author: Gryffindor This panoramic image was created with Autostitch (stitched images may

spots.name: Gülhane Park
spots.summary: Gülhane Park is a historical urban park in the Fatih district of Istanbul, Turkey; it covers an area of 9.7 ha, is adjacent to and on the grounds of the Topkapı Palace. The south entrance of the park sports one of the larger gates of the palace. It is the oldest and one of the most expansive public parks in Istanbul.

spots.name: The Chora
spots.summary: The Chora Church or Kariye Mosque was a Byzantine church, now converted to a mosque, in the Edirnekapı neighborhood of Fatih district, Istanbul, Turkey. It is famous for its outstanding Late Byzantine mosaics and frescos.

names.it: Chiesa di San Salvatore in Chora

spots.name: Sacred Relics
spots.summary: The Islamic Sacred Relics, also known as the Holy Relics, known collectively as the Sacred Trust, consist of religious relics sent to the Ottoman Sultans between the 16th century to the late 19th century.

names.ja: トプカプ宮殿の聖遺物

spots.name: Galata Bridge
spots.summary: The Galata Bridge is a bridge that spans the Golden Horn in Istanbul, Turkey. From the end of the 19th century in particular, the bridge has featured in Turkish literature, theater, poetry and novels.

spots.name: İstiklal Avenue
spots.summary: İstiklal Avenue is a 1.4 kilometre (0.87 mi) pedestrian street in the historic Beyoğlu (Pera) district in Istanbul, Turkey. It is one of the most famous avenues in the city.

spots.name: Column of Constantine
spots.summary: The Column of Constantine is a monumental column commemorating the dedication of Constantinople by Roman emperor Constantine the Great on 11 May 330 AD. Completed c. 328 AD, it is the oldest Constantinian monument to survive in Istanbul.

names.ja: コンスタンティヌスの円柱

spots.name: Bayezid II Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bayezid II Mosque is an early 16th-century Ottoman imperial mosque located in Beyazıt Square in Istanbul, Turkey, near the ruins of the Forum of Theodosius of ancient Constantinople.

spots.name: Milion
spots.summary: The Milion was a marker from which all distances across the Roman Empire were measured. Erected by Septimius Severus in the 3rd century AD in the city of Byzantium, it became the zero-mile marker for the empire upon the re-founding of the city as Constantinople in 330 AD.

photo.author: Gryffindor This panoramic image was created with Autostitch (stitched images may

spots.name: Mihrimah Üsküdar Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mihrimah Sultan Mosque is a 16th century Ottoman mosque overlooking the waterfront in the historic center of the Üsküdar district of Istanbul, Turkey. One of Üsküdar's best-known landmarks, it takes its alternative name from the ferry terminal near which it stands.

names.ja: ミフリマー・スルタン・モスク
names.zh: 米赫里马赫苏丹清真寺

spots.name: Mihrimah Edirnekapı Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mihrimah Sultan Mosque is a 16th-century Ottoman mosque located near the Byzantine land walls in the Edirnekapı neighborhood of Istanbul, Turkey. It was commissioned by Mihrimah Sultan, the daughter of Suleiman the Magnificent and Hürrem Sultan, and designed by the chief imperial architect Mimar Sinan.

names.ja: ミフリマー・スルタン・ジャーミイ (エディルネ門)

spots.name: Column of Justinian
spots.summary: The Column of Justinian was a Roman triumphal column erected in Constantinople by the Byzantine emperor Justinian I in honour of his victories in 543.

spots.name: Church of St. Anthony of Padua
spots.summary: The Church of St. Anthony of Padua, alternatively known as Sant'Antonio di Padova Church or S. Antonio di Padova, is the largest Catholic church in Istanbul, Turkey. It is located on İstiklal Avenue in the Beyoğlu district.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Saint Anthony of Padua, Istanbul

names.es: Iglesia de San Antonio de Padua
names.zh: 伊斯坦布尔帕多瓦的圣安多尼主教座堂

spots.name: Nuruosmaniye Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nuruosmaniye Mosque is an 18th-century Ottoman mosque located in the Çemberlitaş neighbourhood of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey, which was inscribed in the Tentative list of World Heritage Sites in Turkey in 2016.

names.zh: 奴鲁奥斯玛尼耶清真寺

spots.name: Yedikule Fortress

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Yedikule Fortress is a fortified historic structure located in the Yedikule neighbourhood of Fatih, in Istanbul, Turkey.

spots.name: Haydarpaşa railway station
spots.summary: Haydarpaşa station is a railway station in Istanbul, that was, until 2012 the main city terminal for trains travelling to and from the Anatolian side of Turkey. It used to be Turkey's busiest railway station.

spots.name: Çırağan Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Çırağan Palace, a former Ottoman palace, is now a five-star hotel in the Kempinski Hotels chain. It is located on the European shore of the Bosporus, between Beşiktaş and Ortaköy in Istanbul, Turkey.

photo.author: This Photo was taken by Wolfgang Moroder. Feel free to use my photos, but please

spots.name: Yıldız Palace
spots.summary: Yıldız Palace is a vast complex of former imperial Ottoman pavilions and villas in Beşiktaş, Istanbul, Turkey, built in the 19th and early 20th centuries. It was used as a residence by the sultan and his court in the late 19th century.

spots.name: Little Hagia Sophia
spots.summary: The Little Hagia Sophia mosque, formerly the Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus, is a former Greek Orthodox church dedicated to the Syrian Christian Saints Sergius and Bacchus in Constantinople.

names.ja: 聖セルギオス＝バッコス教会

spots.name: Fountain of Ahmed III
spots.summary: The Fountain of Sultan Ahmed III is a fountain in the great square in front of the Imperial Gate of Topkapı Palace in Istanbul, Turkey. It was built under Ottoman sultan Ahmed III in 1728, in the style of the Tulip period. It was a social centre and gathering place during the Ottoman period of Constantinople.

spots.name: Çamlıca Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grand Çamlıca Mosque is a landmark complex for Islamic worship which was completed and opened on 7 March 2019. The mosque stands astride Çamlıca Hill in the Üsküdar district of Istanbul and is visible from much of the centre of the city. The complex incorporates an art gallery, library, and conference hall.

spots.name: Kılıç Ali Pasha Complex

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kılıç Ali Pasha Mosque is a mosque at the heart of a complex designed and built between 1580 and 1587 by Mimar Sinan, who at the time was in his 90s. The mosque itself was constructed in 1578–1580.

names.ja: クルチ・アリ・パシャ・ジャーミィ
names.zh: 奇力克阿里帕夏建築群

spots.name: Beylerbeyi Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Beylerbeyi Palace is a 19th-century Ottoman palace located in the Beylerbeyi neighborhood of Istanbul’s Üsküdar district, on the Asian shore of the Bosporus. Commissioned by Sultan Abdulaziz and completed between 1861 and 1865, the palace served as a summer residence and a place to host foreign dignitaries.

spots.name: Church of St. George
spots.summary: The Patriarchal Cathedral Church of St. George is the principal Eastern Orthodox cathedral located in Istanbul, Turkey, formerly Constantinople.

names.ja: 聖ゲオルギオス大聖堂

spots.name: Walled Obelisk
spots.summary: The Walled Obelisk or Masonry Obelisk is a Roman monument in the form of an obelisk in the former Hippodrome of Constantinople, now Sultanahmet Square in Istanbul, Turkey.

spots.name: Tünel
spots.summary: The Tünel is a historic underground rubber-tyred funicular line in Istanbul, Turkey. It has two stations, connecting Karaköy and Beyoğlu. The tunnel runs uphill from near the confluence of the Golden Horn with the Bosphorus and is about 573 metres long.

spots.name: Ibrahim Pasha Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ibrahim Pasha Palace is an Ottoman imperial court residence of Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha. It is located in Sultanahmet Square of Fatih district in Istanbul, Turkey. Currently, the building is mainly used as the Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum.

spots.name: Augustaion
spots.summary: The Augustaion or, in Latin, Augustaeum, was an important ceremonial square in ancient and medieval Constantinople, roughly corresponding to the modern Aya Sofya Meydanı.

spots.name: Şemsi Pasha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Şemsi Pasha Mosque is an Ottoman mosque located in the large and densely populated district of Üsküdar, in Istanbul, Turkey.

names.ja: シェムシ・パシャ・モスク

spots.name: Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum
spots.summary: The Turkish and Islamic Arts Museum is a museum in Sultanahmet Square in Fatih district of Istanbul, Turkey which first opened in 1914 and in 1983 moved into the palace of Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha, the second grand vizier of Suleiman the Magnificent. The building was constructed in 1524.

names.nl: Museum voor Turkse en Islamitische Kunst
names.de: Museum für türkische und islamische Kunst

spots.name: French Institute
spots.summary: They have good art exhibits for free and sometimes have French films in the cinema.

spots.name: Galata Convent of Whirling Dervishes

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: A ritual dancing hall of the mystical Mevlevi order, the followers of the teachings of Mewlānā Rumi. The quiet and peaceful garden is a welcome escape from the hustle and bustle of Beyoğlu. The oldest Mevlevi lodge in Istanbul, the convent was started in 1491, when the surrounding area was, hard to believe today but, pure wilderness beyond the city walls of Galata, although the current building da

names.zh: 加拉塔梅夫拉维博物馆

spots.name: Museum of the History of Science and Technology in Islam
spots.summary: Museum in a restored building that was the stables for Topkapı Palace. It exhibits various instruments for astronomy, clocks, pumps, weaponry, a steam-powered döner spit, and so on developed in Islamic realms down the centuries, but these are modern repro, and explanations of their context are skimpy. Islamic science and technology preceded that of Europe, as they insist, but they get the tone wro

names.de: Museum für islamische Wissenschafts- und Technologiegeschichte Istanbul
names.ja: イスラム科学技術歴史博物館

spots.name: Beylerbeyi
spots.summary: is a small port with a popular fishing dock. There are many restaurants: those on the port-side serve alcohol and are moderately expensive, those down the side-streets are cheaper. Notable buildings include the 18th-century Hamid-i Evvel mosque, and the 19th-century highway tunnel (which is closed as of Dec 2018). But the standout attraction is the palace.

spots.name: Phanar Greek Orthodox College

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is the red-brick castle seen south of St George. Built 1881/83, it teaches the standard Turkish curriculum plus Greek language and culture, and the tower houses an observatory. No visits.

spots.name: Crimean Memorial Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A neo-gothic Anglican cathedral which would not be out of place in northwestern Europe, the Crimean Memorial Church was built for the Protestant community of the city by [[United Kingdom

spots.name: Bereket Döner

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A quite good value restaurant featuring döner (also on the plate as opposed to the usual wrap/sandwich variety; dipped in tomato sauce to the point of swimming) and traditional Turkish cuisine. The restaurant is a self-service one, i.e., you take a tray, and order your food by pointing at the entrance, and pay at the cash register right next to the food display (take your tableware and bread at th

spots.name: Ficcin
spots.summary: The restaurant offers an exceptional value lunch, but is also pleasantly busy at night. Several of the staff speak English and foreign tourists are welcome alongside the many locals who eat there regularly. Fıccın is unusual in being a Circassian restaurant, which also serves Turkish food. Seats are available on the street and in several rooms inside. Alcohol is also served.

spots.name: Zeytuna

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Lebanese kitchen, from familiar, like falafel and hummus, to offbeat, like mutabal eggplant or mousaka chicken. Alcohol includes signature cocktails, named after Lebanon cities. There is a main hall and a bar, and the latter regularly hosts tango and salsa lessons, live blues, sometimes theatrical performances and film screenings.

spots.name: Pierre Loti

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An open air café on a hill overlooking the Golden Horn in Eyüp. It’s rumored that the French writer the place is named after used to love visiting this café during his residence in Istanbul. The cable car up here offers some nice views. It’s also possible to walk uphill or to take a taxi.

spots.name: Vefa Bozacısı
spots.summary: Established in 1876, this cafe specializes in boza, a ferment of bulgur wheat with a sweetish tart taste. A favourite of the Ottomans, it's still popular in the Balkans and Central Asia. It's less than 1% alcohol, but it was the closest you got to being off your head in Neolithic times.

spots.name: İbrahim Hakkı Uğrak Börek
spots.summary: A bit off the tourist track, the stone oven of this börek shop gives its products a distinctive flavour. Good value and friendly staff. Opens early, but not all varieties of börek will be ready first thing in the morning—the peynirli böreği is usually amongst the first out of the oven.

spots.name: Nevizade Street

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One of the most famous streets in Istiklal boulevard. It's narrow, and is mostly known for its meyhane style restaurants, where lively conversation is the main dish on every table, next to fish and Rakı that is.

spots.name: Palatium Cafe & Restaurant
spots.summary: Decent trad food and ice cold beer. Lounge in the comfy bean-bag chairs, and backgammon and Nargileh are available. The restaurant looks down into the foundations of a Roman-era palace.

spots.name: Şampiyon Kokoreç

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A restaurant mostly focused in kokoreç — roasted and finely minced lamb intestines (yeap). It tastes great and is very budget-friendly: only 10 TL/wrap. Try stuffed mussels as well.

spots.name: Ali Usta Çiğ Köfte
spots.summary: Good value Çiǧ köfte (spicy wrap with a vegan tatar) takeaway. Ali the owner is an Instagram celeb for his videos jibing customers, so you may be in a long line.

spots.name: Park Fora

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great seafood, located in Kuruçeşme park right on the edge of the sea, it has a very nice view of the Bosphorus and Bosphorus Bridge. The waiters know English.

spots.name: Akmanoğlu Fırını

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is the bakery where halkas mentioned in the "See" section, as well as a number of other traditional cookies, both sweet and salty, are produced and sold.

spots.name: The House Café
spots.summary: They serve giant salads, main dishes and pizzas pleasing even to the gourmets. The menu is seasonal which allows them to use only the freshest ingredients.

spots.name: Doy Doy Restaurant
spots.summary: Cafe spread over three floors and a roof terrace with views over the sea and Blue Mosque. Good range of Turkish meals and mezes, with veggie choices.

spots.name: Sarayburnu Aile Çay Bahçesi
spots.summary: Open-air cafe on the coast with great views, though the park is grubby. Tea, coffee and many flavours of hubble-bubble.

spots.name: Anadolu Nargile
spots.summary: Shisha / hookah cafe in the courtyard of the former Çorlulu Ali Paşa Medrese, so plenty of Ottoman ambience.

spots.name: Levent

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A neighborhood which is just across the Sapphire of Istanbul and hosts nice bars.

spots.name: Snog Rooftop Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Good bar. But the attraction here is the stunning view.
